questions.question: What is the elementary mechanistic event during the initiation of alkane halogenation by light (hν)?

options.label: A
options.text: Homolytic cleavage of the halogen-halogen bond (e.g., Cl-Cl or Br-Br) to produce two neutral halogen radicals with unpaired electrons.

options.label: B
options.text: Direct insertion of molecular halogen into a C-H bond.

options.label: C
options.text: Heterolytic cleavage to form a halonium cation and halide anion.

options.label: D
options.text: Excitation of the alkane C-C σ bond to a carbocation.

questions.correct_answer: Homolytic cleavage of the halogen-halogen bond (e.g., Cl-Cl or Br-Br) to produce two neutral halogen radicals with unpaired electrons.
questions.explanation: Photons of appropriate wavelength provide the bond dissociation energy required to split the weak halogen-halogen bond homolytically.

questions.question: In the radical bromination of alkanes, what is the rate-determining propagation step?

options.label: A
options.text: Endothermic abstraction of a hydrogen atom from the alkane by a bromine radical (Br•) to form HBr and an alkyl radical (R•).

options.label: B
options.text: Exothermic reaction of the alkyl radical with Br₂ to form alkyl bromide.

options.label: C
options.text: Coordination of bromine radical to the solvent cage.

options.label: D
options.text: Homolytic recombination of two alkyl radicals.

questions.correct_answer: Endothermic abstraction of a hydrogen atom from the alkane by a bromine radical (Br•) to form HBr and an alkyl radical (R•).
questions.explanation: Hydrogen abstraction by bromine radical is endothermic with a substantial activation barrier, dictating reaction rate and selectivity.

questions.question: Which of the following represents a valid radical chain termination step in alkane chlorination?

options.label: A
options.text: Reaction of •CH₃ with Cl₂ to form CH₃Cl and •Cl.

options.label: B
options.text: Abstraction of H from CH₄ by •Cl to form HCl.

options.label: C
options.text: Homolytic cleavage of Cl₂ by heat.

options.label: D
options.text: The coupling of two alkyl radicals (e.g., •CH₃ + •CH₃ → CH₃CH₃) to destroy radical chain carriers.

questions.correct_answer: The coupling of two alkyl radicals (e.g., •CH₃ + •CH₃ → CH₃CH₃) to destroy radical chain carriers.
questions.explanation: Termination steps consume two radical species to form a stable covalent bond without generating new propagating radicals.

questions.question: What is the quantum mechanical origin of torsional strain in the eclipsed conformation of ethane?

options.label: A
options.text: Attractive van der Waals dispersion forces between hydrogens.

options.label: B
options.text: Steric clash between the tiny hydrogen nuclei.

options.label: C
options.text: Spontaneous radical formation at room temperature.

options.label: D
options.text: Electrostatic repulsion between bonding electron pairs in adjacent C-H σ bonds and destabilizing orbital interactions across eclipsed bonds.

questions.correct_answer: Electrostatic repulsion between bonding electron pairs in adjacent C-H σ bonds and destabilizing orbital interactions across eclipsed bonds.
questions.explanation: Eclipsing forces adjacent bonding electron clouds into close proximity, causing ~12 kJ/mol (3 kcal/mol) of torsional strain in ethane.

questions.question: What is the sequence of conformational intermediates during a cyclohexane chair-to-chair ring flip?

options.label: A
options.text: Chair → Cyclopentane + Methylene → Inverted Chair.

options.label: B
options.text: Chair → Planar Hexagon (TS) → Inverted Chair.

options.label: C
options.text: Chair → Envelope → Inverted Chair.

options.label: D
options.text: Chair → Half-Chair (highest energy TS) → Twist-Boat (local minimum) → Boat (transition state) → Twist-Boat → Half-Chair → Inverted Chair.

questions.correct_answer: Chair → Half-Chair (highest energy TS) → Twist-Boat (local minimum) → Boat (transition state) → Twist-Boat → Half-Chair → Inverted Chair.
questions.explanation: The ring flip proceeds through high-energy half-chair conformations (~45 kJ/mol barrier) via a twist-boat intermediate.

questions.question: What causes the energetic destabilization of an axial methyl group in methylcyclohexane?

options.label: A
options.text: Torsional eclipsing between the methyl group and C2 equatorial hydrogen.

options.label: B
options.text: Dipole-dipole repulsion between carbon atoms.

options.label: C
options.text: Angle strain caused by compression of the C-C-C bond angle to 90°.

options.label: D
options.text: Steric repulsion (gauche-like interactions) between the axial methyl group and the two axial hydrogens located at C3 and C5 on the same side of the ring.

questions.correct_answer: Steric repulsion (gauche-like interactions) between the axial methyl group and the two axial hydrogens located at C3 and C5 on the same side of the ring.
questions.explanation: Axial substituents experience steric crowding identical to two gauche-butane interactions (~7.6 kJ/mol destabilization).

questions.question: During thermal cracking of alkanes at 500°C, how do secondary radicals fragment?

options.label: A
options.text: Via electrocyclic ring closure to cycloalkanes.

options.label: B
options.text: Via concerted reductive elimination.

options.label: C
options.text: Via β-scission: homolytic cleavage of a C-C bond beta to the radical carbon, releasing an alkene and a smaller alkyl radical.

options.label: D
options.text: Via α-cleavage producing two carbocations.

questions.correct_answer: Via β-scission: homolytic cleavage of a C-C bond beta to the radical carbon, releasing an alkene and a smaller alkyl radical.
questions.explanation: Beta-scission is the primary pathway by which carbon radicals fragment into smaller alkenes and primary radicals at high temperatures.

questions.question: What is the mechanistic role of the platinum catalyst during the aromatization of cyclohexane?

options.label: A
options.text: Platinum atoms insert sequentially into C-H bonds via oxidative addition, releasing adsorbed H₂ and generating conjugated π bonds.

options.label: B
options.text: Platinum acts as a strong Brønsted base that abstracts protons.

options.label: C
options.text: Platinum undergoes homolytic cleavage into atomic platinum vapor.

options.label: D
options.text: Platinum forms permanent ionic bonds with the cyclohexane ring.

questions.correct_answer: Platinum atoms insert sequentially into C-H bonds via oxidative addition, releasing adsorbed H₂ and generating conjugated π bonds.
questions.explanation: Transition metal surfaces facilitate sequential C-H activation and dehydrogenation through surface-bound organometallic intermediates.

questions.question: Why does cyclopropane undergo ring opening with Br₂ whereas cyclopentane does not?

options.label: A
options.text: Cyclopropane is an antiaromatic planar ring.

options.label: B
options.text: Cyclopropane has a conjugated π system that undergoes EAS.

options.label: C
options.text: Extreme angle strain (60° vs 109.5°) creates weak, bent 'banana bonds' with high p-character that readily attack electrophilic bromine.

options.label: D
options.text: Cyclopentane is a radical initiator that destroys bromine.

questions.correct_answer: Extreme angle strain (60° vs 109.5°) creates weak, bent 'banana bonds' with high p-character that readily attack electrophilic bromine.
questions.explanation: The severe angle strain (~115 kJ/mol) and bent orbital overlap in cyclopropane confer alkene-like reactivity toward electrophiles.

questions.question: Why does radical bromination of isobutane yield >99% tert-butyl bromide, whereas chlorination yields only 36%?

options.label: A
options.text: Chlorine radicals are too large to attack tertiary carbons.

options.label: B
options.text: Isobutane forms a cyclic bromonium ion intermediate.

options.label: C
options.text: Bromination is endothermic with a late transition state resembling the stable 3° radical (Hammond postulate), whereas chlorination has an unselective early TS.

options.label: D
options.text: Bromine reacts through an ionic SN2 mechanism rather than a radical mechanism.

questions.correct_answer: Bromination is endothermic with a late transition state resembling the stable 3° radical (Hammond postulate), whereas chlorination has an unselective early TS.
questions.explanation: According to the Hammond Postulate, endothermic reactions have late transition states that strongly reflect the relative stabilities of intermediate radicals.

questions.question: What is the quantum mechanical origin of torsional strain in the eclipsed conformation of ethane?

questions.correct_answer: Electrostatic repulsion between bonding electron pairs in adjacent C-H σ bonds and destabilizing orbital interactions across eclipsed bonds.
questions.explanation: Eclipsing forces adjacent bonding electron clouds into close proximity, causing ~12 kJ/mol (3 kcal/mol) of torsional strain in ethane.

questions.question: What is the sequence of conformational intermediates during a cyclohexane chair-to-chair ring flip?

questions.question: What causes the energetic destabilization of an axial methyl group in methylcyclohexane?

questions.explanation: Axial substituents experience steric crowding identical to two gauche-butane interactions (~7.6 kJ/mol destabilization).

questions.question: Why does cyclopropane undergo ring opening with Br₂ whereas cyclopentane does not?

options.text: Extreme angle strain (60° vs 109.5°) creates weak, bent 'banana bonds' with high p-character that readily attack electrophilic bromine.

questions.explanation: The severe angle strain (~115 kJ/mol) and bent orbital overlap in cyclopropane confer alkene-like reactivity toward electrophiles.

options.label: D
options.text: Bromination is endothermic with a late transition state resembling the stable 3° radical (Hammond postulate), whereas chlorination has an unselective early TS.

questions.explanation: According to the Hammond Postulate, endothermic reactions have late transition states that strongly reflect the relative stabilities of intermediate radicals.
